reason: The description is largely accurate and covers the core behavior well: radix-based parsing, fixed vs unbounded length, forceLen semantics, numeric separator handling, error callback behavior, accumulation formula, and failure conditions. It correctly identifies the two separator error types and the bailOnError/recovery branching. A few subtle details are missed or slightly off: the description says non-digit/non-letter characters terminate parsing 'unless forceLen requires consuming them, in which case parsing ultimately fails' — but the implementation actually sets val=0 and invalid=true for *any* out-of-radix character when forceLen is true (including letters with val > radix), not just non-digit/non-letter ones. The description also doesn't mention that the loop counter `i` increments but `pos` does not when a separator is skipped (the `continue` path), which is a subtle but implementable detail. The description omits that `forbiddenSiblings` checks apply to the *previous* character as well as the next, and that `Number.isNaN(next)` (end of input) triggers unexpectedNumericSeparator. The description also doesn't mention the `lineStart` and `curLine` parameters passed to error callbacks. These are secondary details that don't undermine the overall accuracy.
missing_functionality: The loop uses a counter `i` (not just `pos`) to bound iterations, so separator skips via `continue` consume a loop iteration without advancing `i` relative to pos — this subtle interaction is not described.
forbiddenSiblings check applies to the *previous* character (prev) as well as next; description only implies neighbor checks without specifying both directions explicitly.
Number.isNaN(next) (i.e., reading past end of input) triggers the unexpectedNumericSeparator path — not mentioned.
lineStart and curLine parameters are passed to all error callbacks but not mentioned in the description.
forceLen sets val=0 and invalid=true for any out-of-radix character (including letters with val > radix, not just non-digit/non-letter characters).
incorrect_or_misleading_points: Description says 'non-digit/non-letter characters terminate parsing unless forceLen requires consuming them' — but forceLen applies to all out-of-radix values (val >= radix), including ASCII letters that are valid digits for lower radices but not the current one, not just non-digit/non-letter characters.

Description implies the `invalidDigit` callback path only applies to 'decimal-style digits invalid for the radix' (val <= 9) — this is correct but the description's phrasing could be clearer that letters with val > 9 that exceed the radix fall through to the forceLen/break path, not the invalidDigit path.
